sounds.intro: Turkish is spelled exactly as it sounds. There are no genders and no articles. Learn the special letters first.
rows: a short, flat "uh", like the "a" in "about"
say "oh" with rounded lips, like German ö
say "ee" with rounded lips, like German ü
silent, makes the vowel before it longer

phrases.title: Formal and informal
phrases.note: sen (informal): friends, family, children. siz (formal): strangers, older people, work. Siz is also "you all". Use siz when unsure.

grammar.title: Pronouns
text: Turkish drops the pronoun most of the time, because the verb ending shows who is speaking. Pronouns are for emphasis.

grammar.title: Singular and plural
text: Add -ler or -lar. Use -ler after e, i, ö, ü, and -lar after a, ı, o, u (vowel harmony). After a number, the noun stays singular: iki kitap (two book).

grammar.title: To be: -im, -sin, -dir
text: There is no separate verb "to be". Add an ending to the noun or adjective. After a vowel, a buffer y appears.

grammar.title: Var and yok: have, there is
text: Turkish says "my X exists" (var) or "my X does not exist" (yok). Ending shows the owner: -im (my), -in (your), -i (his).

grammar.title: Present tense: -iyor
text: Verb stem + -iyor + person ending. Gelmek (to come): gel-iyor-um.

grammar.title: Basic sentences
text: Verb comes last. Order: subject, time, place, object, verb. Adjectives come before the noun.
ex: we live in a big house

grammar.title: Negation
text: Verbs: add -ma / -me after the stem. Nouns and adjectives: değil (is not). Var → yok.
Add -me / -ma before the tense ending: gelmiyorum (I am not coming). Var / yok: "there is / there is not". Değil = is not (for nouns and adjectives): ben öğrenci değilim.
ex: I do not have a car
he does not work on Sundays

grammar.title: Asking questions
text: Add the little word mi / mı / mu / mü after the word you ask about. It follows vowel harmony. No change of word order.

grammar.title: Possessives
text: Add an ending to the noun: -im (my), -in (your), -i (his / her), -imiz (our), -iniz (your pl.), -leri (their). Vowel harmony changes the vowel.

grammar.title: Formal vs informal
text: sen (and -sin, -im) for friends. siz (and -siniz) for strangers, older people, and groups. Add -ler or "Bey" (Mr) / "Hanım" (Mrs) after names for respect.

grammar.title: Past and future (simple)
text: Past: stem + -di + person ending (-m, -n, -, -k, -niz, -ler). Future: stem + -ecek / -acak + person ending.

grammar.title: Commands
text: The informal command is the plain stem: gel! (come), otur! (sit). Polite / plural: stem + -in / -ın / -un / -ün: gelin, oturun. Negative: add -me / -ma: gelme! (do not come).

grammar.title: Can, must, want
text: -ebilmek = can (yüzebilirim), -meli = must (gitmeliyim), istemek = want (yemek istiyorum). Cannot = -ememek (yüzemem). Must not = -memeli (gitmemeliyim).
ex: I do not want to eat

grammar.title: In, on, at
text: Turkish uses endings after the noun: -de / -da = in / at / on (okulda), -e / -a = to (okula), -den / -dan = from. Words like üstünde (on top of), altında (under), yanında (next to), yakınında (near) go after the noun.
ex: the book is on the table
the cat is under the table
the shop is next to the bank
the park is near the station
the key is in the bag

grammar.title: Comparing things
text: daha + adjective = more (daha büyük). en + adjective = the most (en büyük). "than" is shown by -den / -dan on the second thing: benden uzun (taller than me).
